core_obligations: Translate assumption (1) into quasi-compactness of the diagonal Delta_{X/Y} (proof lines 9217-9218).

Show that the diagonal satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion: interpret a solid diagram as a pair of morphisms a, b : Spec(A) -> X over Y and use the uniqueness assumption to get a = b (proof lines 9219-9232).
Apply the converse criterion to conclude that the diagonal is universally closed (proof lines 9232-9234).
Combine universal closedness with local finite typeness, separatedness and monomorphismhood to obtain a finite morphism, hence a closed immersion, hence separatedness of f (proof lines 9235-9244).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma (named 'Valuative criterion separatedness' in the statement): a quasi-separated morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S satisfying the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion is separated (source lines 9204-9215). The proof is a genuine reduction of the hypothesis to the diagonal: quasi-separatedness of f says Delta_{X/Y} is quasi-compact, a solid valuative diagram for Delta_{X/Y} encodes a pair of morphisms Spec(A) -> X over Y whose equality follows from uniqueness for f, so the diagonal satisfies the existence part of the criterion; the converse criterion then makes Delta_{X/Y} universally closed, and combined with it being locally of finite type, separated and a representable monomorphism, this forces it to be a finite closed immersion, i.e. f is separated.
